key_insight: A Transformer model using routine blood tests and diagnosis histories can identify people at elevated pancreatic cancer risk years before diagnosis.
clinical_relevance: This could help enrich screening populations so targeted pancreatic cancer surveillance is more feasible and potentially finds disease earlier.
method: Trained a custom Transformer with multi-head attention on longitudinal coded diagnoses and blood test trajectories.
Used data from 6,017 pancreatic cancer cases and 177,081 controls with up to 12 years of prior medical history.
Tested external generalization with leave-one-site-out validation at 1-, 2-, and 3-year lead times.
evidence_signal: External validation showed AUROC 0.837 at 1 year, 0.797 at 2 years, and 0.760 at 3 years, with good calibration (slope 1.08, Brier score 0.025).
watch_item: Performance was evaluated retrospectively, so real-world usefulness will depend on prospective validation, site transferability, and how screening thresholds affect false positives.
paper_title: Digitally enriching a screening population for pancreatic cancer using routine blood-based measures and clinical histories
